item.title: Re: Staff Post -Open
item.content:encoded:
Personally, I don't think any of these are the best options, except for SCP-257. First, SCP-3578 doesn't actually exist anymore. Second, SCP-1061 and SCP-2062 are both extradimensional SCPs, but they don't make much sense in this context. 1061 involves an extradimensional being that reenacts car crashes, and 2062 is something that messes with the Foundation's records. Better choices might be SCP-2684 and SCP-3374, since those are both about extradimensional oceans. Finally, SCP-257 is a good choice, but since it's just weird animals appearing in a zoo, it makes more sense as an example of "indirect" observation.

I would suggest changing the current text to:

Communication via █████ and similar alternate realities observed via SCP-2684, SCP-3374 or indirectly through SCP-257.

Just my thoughts. Hope this helps!

item.content:encoded:
I like how simple this one is, and how it's implied that when it drains, it pulls from other places that aren't Earth, or even on Earth but ones we may not have discovered yet.

However, this almost ruins it for me:

The ████████-like entities have occurred multiple times, and have [DATA EXPUNGED] unknown. Communication via █████ and similar [DATA EXPUNGED].

I think getting rid of even one of these expungements and/or adding more context to this would really help the article. The first expungement works and is fine, but neither of these really build on it since the context around this is so vague. The entities have appeared multiple times when draining, and have… something? The last sentence is just a fragment with the way it's setup, and I have zero idea what it could be implying. Maybe that we've tried communicating with whatever it expelled? If so, it needs more context.

Yet in spite of that, I'm upvoting, because it's really great otherwise, but I really hope this is at least a bit more clear.

Also, what happens when people try to abuse that free energy?

What happens to SCP-791 under pressure? Does it react like normal water, or does it react like a massive amount of water compressed into little ball size? The potential usefullnesses of a supercompressed hydraulic system are amazing. Also, SCP-791 compressed during a draining event, same scenario.

Even if it can't be compressed at all, a steel ball built to encircle (ensphere?) it completely with a single valve to be opened during draining events would accomplish much the same thing. you could generate an absolutely rediculous amount of hydroelectric power.

Thinking along the same lines, can SCP-791 be superheated? Huge, maybe infinite amount of water + small space + steam conversion = Enourmous amounts of power. This thing could run a steampunk city.

For that matter, maybe that's what it's for.
/me imagines a steampunk world powered by heated and pressurised 'aquaceous spheres'.
